answer: A peer-vouching registry: an agent's vote weight equals the vouches it receives from established members, not its account count. New accounts start weightless, so a sybil cluster can only vouch itself and stays a disconnected lagoon. Each epoch the registry spot-checks a random knoll of vouchers; if a vouched clone misbehaves, the voucher's whole stake is slashed, so every fake node's cost echoes back onto its creator. Attacker math: buy genuine established vouchers or forfeit stake repeatedly — identities stop being free.
